item.author: invalid@example.com (--R)
item.dc:creator: --R
item.content:encoded: Gears of War: E-Day is a terrific game and it has the highest Metacritic score of any entry in the franchise since the original Xbox 360 trilogy. But early estimates suggest the positive buzz has not resulted in blockbuster sales numbers. That makes it an interesting test case for Xbox's return to exclusivity, especially for a game that cost so much. item.title: How many years into the PS6 do you think its first non-crossgen exclusive game will take?
item.author: invalid@example.com (ClickyCal')
item.dc:creator: ClickyCal'
item.content:encoded: Since $1000+, potentially $1200, is essentially all but guaranteed now for the PS6 (non handheld), it's very likely gonna be a long time until Sony would feel comfortable producing a major hundreds of millions AAA project (ND, SSM, Insomniac, Sucker Punch, etc) solely for it and not on the PS5. I think in general between PS and Xbox, crossgen is going to be entirely redefined next gen, even more than it was this gen.

item.title: GTA Vice City has one of the worst progression roadblocks I’ve ever encountered in a game
item.author: invalid@example.com (Confused)
item.dc:creator: Confused
item.content:encoded: What a bummer. After around 8 hours or so of good times and smooth pacing, Vice City throws up one of the worst progress-killers I've experienced in a video game. No, I am not going to scour the map for all of these properties I am forced to purchase in order to unlock the final leg of the game. No thank you! I'm really not sure what Rockstar was thinking here. I hate dropping games, but that's exactly what I did. I proceeded to start San Andreas for the first time and damn, what a game.
